special.NOTES:
Auto-focus information used by many older Canon models.  The values in this
        record are sequential, and some have variable sizes based on the value of
        NumAFPoints (which may be 1,5,7,9,15,45 or 53).  The AFArea coordinates are
        given in a system where the image has dimensions given by AFImageWidth and
        AFImageHeight, and 0,0 is the image center. The direction of the Y axis
        depends on the camera model, with positive Y upwards for EOS models, but
        apparently downwards for PowerShot models.

fields.Name: ValidAFPoints
fields.Notes: number of AF points valid in the following information

fields.Name: AFImageWidth
fields.Notes: size of image in AF coordinates

special.NOTES:
Newer version of the AFInfo record containing much of the same information
        (and coordinate confusion) as the older version.  In this record, NumAFPoints
        may be 7, 9, 11, 19, 31, 45 or 61, depending on the camera model.

fields.Name: ValidAFPoints
fields.Notes: number of AF points valid in the following information

fields.Name: AFImageWidth
fields.Notes: size of image in AF coordinates

PrintConv.1: Adjust all by the same amount

special.NOTES:
Most recent record from the ring of AF tracking records in the EOS R1 and R5
        Mark II CameraInfo.

fields.Name: AFFocusPosition
fields.Notes: lens focus position in arbitrary units

fields.Name: AFSamplingRate
fields.Notes:
rate of the AF tracking records, confirmed by their timestamps.  Usually 60,
            but drops to 30, 15 or 8 when the live view image is dark

fields.Name: AFFocusDistance
fields.Notes:
focus distance from AF as the lower edge of a table step (the next step up
            is the upper limit), same as the FocusDistanceLower of the lens data.
            0 before AF reports a distance, "inf" for 65526.  It is a coarse step
            (for example 1380, 1550, 1750, 1970, 2220, 2510, 2850 ... mm), the finer
            value is in AFFocusPosition

fields.Name: AFDetectedSubject
fields.Notes:
class of the subject found by subject detection.  The animal classes were
            identified by photographing a cat, a dog, a bird and a horse.  The camera
            often gets the class wrong for birds, which have been seen with all three

fields.Name: AFTrackingTarget
fields.Notes: part of the detected subject that AF was tracking

fields.Name: AFTrackingArea
fields.Notes:
centre X, centre Y, width and height of the tracked area, in AF image
            coordinates with the origin at the top left

fields.Name: AFEyeUsed
fields.Notes:
"Left" and "Right" match the Left Eye and Right Eye settings of
            EyeDetection.  "Unresolved" when only one eye was found

special.NOTES:

fields.Name: AFTrackingHistory
fields.Notes:
the whole ring of 12 AF tracking records, newest first, one entry per
            record: time before the newest record, tracking target, detected parts, eye
            used, tracked area (centre X, centre Y, width, height), the unsmoothed
            centre of the tracked area (X, Y relative to the image centre, not fully
            decoded), and the AF focus distance step and focus position (see
            AFFocusDistance and AFFocusPosition), three raw focus error samples, and two
            millisecond timers (since the start of AF, and since the shutter release of
            the latest frame, not fully decoded). Each record holds a single box (the
            tracked part), so the boxes of the other detected parts are not available.
            Records with another layout are skipped. The records are samples of the AF
            tracking taken at the AF rate (AFSamplingRate, usually 60 Hz, lower when the
            live view image is dark), not the shooting rate, and each sample has a time
            stamp, so the rings of the frames of a burst overlap and can be joined by
            that time stamp into one continuous history (at 30 fps a sample is stored in
            up to 7 frames).  opies of a sample are identical except for the newest
            samples of the first frames of a burst, where the same time stamp can appear
            in several slots with different bytes that are not decoded; the decoded
            values do not change, and the newest slot is the latest revision

fields.Name: FormatFileNumber

fields.Name: LensDiaphragmCount
fields.Notes:
Not valid for the lenses with the second layout (see LensDriveCount3).
            Counts diaphragm drive commands:  each exposure stopped down from the
            maximum aperture adds 2 (close and reopen), while exposures at the maximum
            aperture add none, and so do the frames of a focus-bracketing run, during
            which the diaphragm stays closed.  Each lens start-up opens the diaphragm
            fully and returns it to the set aperture, adding a varying number of counts.
            Long focus moves add a few counts too

fields.Name: LensAFCount
fields.Notes:
Not valid for the lenses with the second layout (see LensDriveCount3).
            Counts focus drive commands, not the distance moved:  each focus-bracketing
            step adds 1 at any step size or aperture, an AF operation or a manual focus
            move by wire adds about 2, each lens start-up adds about 3, and stopped-down
            exposures add none.  Manual-focus lenses (eg. TS-E 24mm f/3.5L II) set the
            high bit (0x800000), shown as "Not supported"

fields.Name: LensISCount
fields.Notes:
Appears to count IS unit start-ups:  each lens power-on adds 1, even with
            the IS switch off, each flip of the IS switch adds 1 or 2, and shooting,
            focus bracketing included, adds none.  Only extracted when the LensModel
            name contains IS, since some lenses without IS fill this position with
            other values.  Not written by some lenses with IS (eg. RF 600mm F11 and
            RF 800mm F11)

fields.Name: LensDriveCount3
fields.Notes:
Only for the lenses with the second LensInfo layout, where offsets 7-8 are
            zero (eg. RF 28-70mm F2.8 IS STM and RF 45mm F1.2 STM).  A lifetime counter
            that increases by about 3-4 per power-on and does not follow the number of
            shots.  What it counts is unconfirmed

special.NOTES: Custom picture style information for various models.
Custom picture style information for the EOS 5DmkIII, 60D, 600D and 1100D.

fields.Name: Sharpness
fields.Notes: all models except the 20D and 350D

fields.Name: WBShiftAB
fields.Notes: positive is a shift toward amber

fields.Name: WBShiftGM
fields.Notes: positive is a shift toward green

fields.Name: BlackMaskLeftBorder
fields.Notes:
coordinates for the area to the left or right of the image used to calculate
            the average black level

fields.Name: InternalSerialNumber2
fields.Notes: could be the number on a barcode sticker of the main circuit board

fields.Name: AutoISO
fields.Notes: actual ISO used = BaseISO * AutoISO / 100

fields.Name: MeasuredEV
fields.Notes:
this is the Canon name for what could better be called MeasuredLV, and
            should be close to the calculated LightValue for a proper exposure with most
            models

fields.Name: SequenceNumber
fields.Notes: valid only for some models

fields.Name: OpticalZoomCode
fields.Notes: for many PowerShot models, a this is 0-6 for wide-tele zoom

fields.Name: CameraTemperature
fields.Notes: newer EOS models only

fields.Name: AFPointsInFocus
fields.Notes: used by D30, D60 and some PowerShot/Ixus models

fields.Name: FocusDistanceUpper
fields.Notes: FocusDistance tags are only extracted if FocusDistanceUpper is non-zero

fields.Name: FlashOutput
fields.Notes:
used only for PowerShot models, this has a maximum value of 500 for models
            like the A570IS

special.NOTES: Information found in the "skip" atom of Canon MOV videos.
This information is found in images from newer EOS models.

fields.Name: OriginalImageWidth
fields.Notes: full size of original image before being rotated or scaled in camera
